extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, patent practitioners, and other USPTO stakeholders (competitors, public commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and a proposed-rule change from the USPTO governing the use of terminal disclaimers to overcome nonstatutory (obviousness-type) double patenting, including a new enforceability condition and procedural details for public comment. Relevant to how practitioners draft, file, and litigate patents tied by terminal disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness-type double patenting (nonstatutory double patenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under U.S. law, an inventor, patent owner or joint researchers may obtain more than one patent with claims that vary in only minor (patentably indistinct) ways from each other. The USPTO will reject such claims under “obviousness-type double patenting” (also known as “nonstatutory double patenting”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will allow claims to issue only as long as the practice of obtaining similar claims across patents isn’t used to extend the patent exclusivity term or allow multiple parties to harass an alleged infringer. This standard is intended to balance incentivizing innovation while providing certainty to competitors and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of terminal disclaimers to obviate nonstatutory double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminal disclaimers are filed to obviate (overcome) nonstatutory double patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically, filing a terminal disclaimer has been a method for patentees to overcome an obviousness-type double patenting rejection; the proposed rule would add an additional requirement to that practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed third condition for terminal disclaimers (enforceability requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To overcome double patenting the patentee would need to agree that the patent with the terminal disclaimer will be enforceable only if the patent is not tied and has never been tied through one or more terminal disclaimers to a patent in which any claim has been finally held unpatentable or invalid over prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This new enforceability condition is intended to reduce the cost of separately challenging each patent in a group of multiple patents directed to indistinct variations of a single invention, streamline and expedite patent disputes, narrow validity issues, and provide greater certainty to competitors and the public. The precise scope and application would be defined in the final rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective application of the proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule is prospective in nature and would apply to terminal disclaimers filed on or after the effective date of any final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentees will need to consider and potentially adapt their practices for terminal disclaimers going forward; existing terminal disclaimers filed before the effective date would not be governed by this new requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy objectives and limits on terminal disclaimer use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office's application of these standards aims to 'strike a balance between incentivizing innovation in the first instance while providing more certainty to competitors and the public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating terminal disclaimers and double patenting practices, consider whether the practice extends exclusivity or permits harassment, and whether rule changes would reduce costs, streamline disputes, and promote competition. The USPTO frames changes as 'surgical' adjustments to reduce costs while preserving incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment process and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on the proposed rule, as well as comments on USPTO practice as related to the proposed rule, are welcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must submit comments on the NPRM by July 9 through the Federal eRulemaking Portal to ensure consideration. Stakeholders may provide feedback on both the proposed regulatory text and related USPTO practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO support and stakeholder adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: While the USPTO moves forward with rulemaking, the Office is considering ways the Office can support stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that, as with any proposed rule change, patentees will need to consider and potentially adapt their practices; the Office may provide support or guidance during the transition.
